bounded_statement: Within the supplied files for this case only: the workflow enters all 24 leaf-disc rows (3 discs from each of 8 saplings) as separate observations into scipy.stats.fisher_exact, a procedure whose sampling model treats every table entry as an independent unit, while the data description designates sapling_id as the independent unit. This repeated entry of the same independent unit inflates the effective sample size from 8 saplings to 24 discs and produces the report's selected result (two-sided p = 0.0391, declared significant at alpha = 0.05). An analysis at the declared independent-unit level (per-sapling majority outcome: saturated 3 necrotic-majority of 4 vs drained 1 of 4; Fisher 2x2 [[3,1],[1,3]]) gives two-sided p = 34/70 ≈ 0.486, so the stated significance claim is not supported once row dependence within saplings is respected. This assessment is bounded to the provided task, data, workflow, and report; no external data or cross-case information was used.

counterevidence_considered.description: The data description also states 'One trial is: one row', which could be read as sanctioning a per-row (per-disc) analysis. However, the same description names sapling_id as the independent-unit column, so trials sharing a sapling are repeated measures of one independent unit, and this reading does not license treating rows as independent in a row-independent test.

evidence.description: The workflow builds the 2x2 table by iterating over every disc row and incrementing counts, then feeds these disc-level counts to fisher_exact, a row-independent procedure, with no aggregation by sapling_id anywhere in the analysis path.

The report's selected result claims significance based on the 24 disc-level observations (p = 0.0391), i.e., the conclusion rests directly on the pseudoreplicated sample size. Independently verified: the 9/3 vs 3/9 table gives two-sided Fisher p = 105802/2704156 ≈ 0.0391, matching the report; the sapling-level table (majority outcome per sapling, [[3,1],[1,3]]) gives p = 34/70 ≈ 0.486, not significant.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the issue claim in three ways. (1) Could the disc-level test be valid because discs are actually independent? No: the regime is applied at the pot/sapling level and discs share a sapling's physiology; empirically, 4 of 8 saplings show all three discs with identical outcomes, consistent with strong within-sapling correlation rather than independence. (2) Could the significance conclusion survive an analysis at the declared independent-unit level? I recomputed both tests analytically. Disc level: table [[9,3],[3,9]], two-sided Fisher p = 2*(C(12,9)C(12,3)+C(12,10)C(12,2)+C(12,11)C(12,1)+C(12,12)C(12,0))/C(24,12) = 105802/2704156 ≈ 0.0391, confirming the report's number. Sapling level (majority-necrotic per sapling: saturated 3/4 vs drained 1/4, table [[3,1],[1,3]]): two-sided p = 34/70 ≈ 0.486; even the most extreme possible 8-unit table ([[4,0],[0,4]]) gives p = 2/70 ≈ 0.0286, showing the observed sapling-level data are nowhere near that. So the significance claim does not survive correction. (3) Could the workflow contain hidden clustering adjustment I missed? I read the full analysis.py: contingency() tallies raw rows, fisher_exact is called once on those tallies, and sapling_id is used only for cosmetic counts in build_report; there is no aggregation, mixed model, or cluster correction. All three falsification routes failed, so the issue stands as demonstrated.

root_cause: The contingency() function in workflow/analysis.py tallies every CSV row (one leaf disc) directly into the 2x2 moisture-regime-by-outcome table, and fisher_exact is applied to those disc-level counts. Because three discs are punched from each sapling and the moisture regime is applied at the sapling level, the discs are repeated, correlated measurements of the same authorized independent unit (sapling_id). Fisher's exact test conditions on margins under an independence-of-observations model, so counting each disc as a separate observation triples the apparent sample size (24 instead of 8) and understates the p-value. The observed within-sapling clustering of outcomes (e.g., CH01 and CH02 entirely necrotic; CH07 and CH08 entirely intact) confirms the rows are not independent. No aggregation to sapling level or cluster-aware method was applied anywhere in the workflow.
